researcher_notes: 5 files. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE CAVEAT: four of the five are print-to-PDF captures of balyo.com product PAGES, not engineering datasheets — the nav bar ('Autonomous Forklifts / Solutions / Software / ROI / Company / Contact'), the 'Book a Demo' button and the '© 2026 Balyo' footer are all captured. They are still first-party manufacturer material and the headline stat blocks (Load capacity / Lift Height / Aisle width) are explicit printed figures, but there is no VDI 2198 table and no page numbering, so citations below reference the on-page section heading instead of a page number. The fifth file (Veeny_-_VNA_Datasheet_-_11112021.pdf) IS a real datasheet, dated 01/2020 in its footer. That file's embedded text layer is corrupted (every glyph is duplicated/interleaved, producing strings like '11 1 4 5154451475 1/4 064 0/ ,57799,1'); it was read by rendering p.1 with pdftoppm at 160 dpi instead — all Veeny values below come from the rendered image of the printed spec table, which is legible and unambiguous. VARIANT-SPLIT RECOMMENDATION: the DB holds a single merged row 'LOWY / LOWY HD', but Balyo publishes two SEPARATE product pages with materially different numbers (lift 2.9 m vs 3 m, aisle 2.9 m vs 2950 mm) and the LOWY HD page explicitly names LOWY HD as a distinct machine that 'collaborates with other autonomous robots such as REACHY and VEENY'. Recorded as two entries; the merged row's stored values match neither cleanly. This is a proposal, not a resolution.

products.notes: CONFLICT 1 — min_aisle_width: DB holds 2700 mm; this page states 'FROM 2.9m / 10ft' = 2900 mm. Do not overwrite. Neither the LOWY nor the LOWY HD page supports 2700; the nearest published figure on any Balyo page in this batch is REACHY's 2900. CONFLICT 2 — safety_coverage: DB holds 'Single plane (2D)'; this page states a top-mounted 3D lidar using '64 planes of data ... across all three planes' = Full 3D. Note the DB already stores 'Full 3D' for LOWY CB and REACHY off the SAME boilerplate sentence, so the LOWY row looks like an inconsistency rather than a real difference. CONFLICT 3 (only if the merged row is kept) — lifting_height: DB holds 3000 mm, which is the LOWY HD figure; the plain LOWY page says 2.9 m / 2.93 m. If the split is accepted this resolves itself. LOAD TYPE — this page consistently says 'open pallets' ('LOWY efficiently manages all OPEN pallet movements', 'station transfers using open pallets'), in explicit contrast to the LOWY CB page which says 'open and closed pallets'. AP0 has no open-vs-closed pallet field in Forklift scope (free_lift_open_closed_pallet is a Boolean in AMR scope), so this differentiator is not storable. DRIVE_TYPE flagged, not changed: the DB holds 'Reach Truck', but this page calls the machine a 'Stacker' throughout and never mentions a reach mast — Balyo's reach truck is a separate product (REACHY). 'Straddle Stacker' would be the closer AP0 value, but the page states no chassis geometry, so nothing is proposed. NOT STATED anywhere on this page and therefore left null: max_speed, battery_type, operating temperatures, dimensions, vda5050_compatible, integration_capability, min_total_height, turning radius. The DB's battery_type=Li-Ion, vda5050_compatible=1 and the 8-value integration_capability list are not sourced from this document.

products.notes: NOTE ON THE 2950 mm AISLE FIGURE — this is the ONLY aisle width in the whole Balyo batch printed natively in millimetres rather than rounded metres, so it is the most trustworthy of the five and is a good anchor for judging the others (LOWY 2.9 m, LOWY CB 3.4 m, REACHY 2.9 m, VEENY 1800 mm). PAGE-TITLE COLLISION (why this file could plausibly have been merged): the LOWY HD page's <title>/H1 is literally 'LOWY Stacker AGV/AMR' — identical to the plain LOWY page. The two are distinguishable only by the filename, the sub-headline ('Heavy Load Pallet Movement and Storage Autonomy' vs 'Heavy Load Autonomy for Warehouses and Manufacturing'), the stat block, and the body text, which names 'LOWY HD' 11 times. This is very likely why the DB merged them, and is worth recording as a Balyo document convention. Same payload as the plain LOWY (1600 kg) despite the 'Heavy Duty' name — the differentiator is described as 'heavy duty LOW-LIFT applications', not a higher payload. PAYLOAD OPTION NOT SPLIT: the 1,200 kg / 2,600 lbs version is a published option but carries no separate model designation, so it is documented here rather than created as a product. (Note Balyo's own imperial figures are loose: 2,600 lbs = 1179 kg and 3,530 lbs = 1601 kg — the metric figures are the reliable ones.) The DB's max_payload = 1600 correctly reflects the top option. LOWY CB is the only machine in this batch that explicitly handles CLOSED pallets — 'both open-type and closed-type pallets' — which is a real differentiator against LOWY / LOWY HD but has no Forklift-scope AP0 field. products.notes: CONFLICT 1 (most significant in this batch) — lifting_height: DB holds 17200 mm; this datasheet states 14710 mm pick / 14510 mm drop, both printed with internally consistent imperial conversions (579.1 in and 571.2 in), and both stated TWICE (FOCUS paragraph + spec table). A digit error on Balyo's side is very unlikely. The datasheet footer is dated '01 / 2020' and the filename says 11112021, so the DB's 17200 may come from a newer product generation — but nothing in this document supports it. Difference is 2.5–2.7 m on a hard K.O. field; needs resolution against the current product page, not resolvable from the corpus. CONFLICT 2 — battery_type: DB holds Li-Ion, this sheet states 'Energy : Lead-Acid' as a flat single value with no options list. Per the false-positive checklist this is NOT a VDI-standard-config row (there is no VDI table here and no 'standard unit only' disclaimer), so it reads as exclusive — but it is a 2020 sheet and Balyo's four other 2026-era pages all offer Li-Ion, so this is plausibly generational drift rather than a real contradiction. Flagged, not resolved. CONFLICT 3 (minor, recorded for completeness) — max_speed: DB holds 2.2 m/s, sheet states 2 m/s. Note the sheet's qualifier '(with 360° Safety)' on all three speed rows, which implies a higher unrestricted speed exists; 2.2 may be that figure. Low-stakes (SCORING field), probably not worth a cycle. DB DATA-QUALITY FLAG (unrelated to this document) — the VEENY row stores max_gradient = 0.0. Per the project's Blank ≠ Zero invariant a literal 0 % gradeability is almost certainly a null that was written as zero; this document states no gradient at all. MIN_TOTAL_HEIGHT DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL: the sheet prints 'Overall height (except mast) — 2555 mm' and 'Navigation laser height — 2326 mm', but AP0 defines min_total_height as the lowest overall vehicle height MAST COLLAPSED, and the collapsed-mast height of a 14.5 m turret truck is nowhere on this sheet. Writing 2555 would understate a KO_IF_GT field by many metres. NOT MAPPED (no AP0 field): weight without battery 10615 kg / 23402 lbs; lateral reach 1355 mm; front safety field height 165 mm; lateral safety field height 400 mm; lateral speed 0,6 m/s; navigation laser height 2326 mm. ROWS THAT READ 'Depending upon configuration' and are therefore genuinely null: overall width, overall length, side shift range magnitude, and maximum weight at maximum stacking height (the last is the payload-derating figure — same structural gap flagged on the Toyota SAI125CB in this session, and here Balyo declines to publish it at all). SAFETY: the sheet says '360° Smart Safety System' — 360° describes horizontal coverage, not vertical, so it does not by itself justify the DB's 'Limited 3D (e.g. waterfall)'; left untouched. No PL level, no ISO 3691-4 reference appears on this sheet, so the DB's functional_safety_level=PLd and safety_standard='ISO 3691-4 (verify)' are not sourced here. GUIDANCE: DB holds 'Rail|Wire'; this sheet mentions neither, and its 'infrastructure-free navigation' claim arguably sits in tension with wire guidance. Not flagged as a conflict (VNA rail guidance is a common site-side option that a product sheet may simply omit), but worth a look.
